first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (simplify_onboarding and shorten-onboarding) show durable, retention-neutral lifts in activation for self-serve/SMB accounts—directly addressing the observed metric declines. Promotional pricing, despite competitive pressure, is explicitly flagged in memory_73 as harmful to 30-day retention and not generalizable; chasing the competitor's price war risks trading long-term qualified revenue for short-term acquisition, which conflicts with the primary objective. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are viable but don't address the acute onboarding/activation drop this week, and activation_messaging targets a later funnel stage than the onboarding completion drop. I verify memory_31 and memory_86 because they are the two most similar and potentially overlapping memories supporting the same action, and confirming their original scope (segment, definition of 'shorten/simplify') reduces risk of misapplying a self-serve-specific finding too broadly. Running this as a standard (not broad) experiment preserves the ability to observe downstream retention effects before scaling, consistent with the caution shown around memory_73.

final.rationale: Both source records confirm the inherited memories without material caveats beyond scope. exp_31 shows signup simplification lifts activation (+9%) and qualified revenue (+4%) for SMB with only a negligible retention dip (-1%), and it's explicitly confirmed for the SMB segment, which matches the current context (SMB is the segment under competitive pressure and where activation/onboarding declines are occurring). exp_86 shows shortened onboarding improves completion and time-to-value while actually improving 30-day retention (+3%), making it retention-positive and low-risk. Combining a signup-simplification-style change with a shortened onboarding flow directly targets both observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) using two independently confirmed, complementary, retention-safe mechanisms. This is preferable to promotional_pricing, which per memory_73 drives acquisition at the cost of retention and is explicitly flagged as not generalizable — chasing the competitor on price risks short-term revenue at the expense of the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I'm running this as a standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_31 notes non-replication outside SMB, so scope should stay bounded while we confirm the combined effect and watch retention, even though individual components showed retention-neutral-to-positive results.
